The node text is verbatim as quoted, and the statement it makes is false: over an ordinary point of characteristic p the fibre has two subgroups of order p, the infinitesimal ker F and an etale one. I recomputed the red team's counterexample independently: for y^2 = x^3 + 3x + 2 over F_5, 4a^3 + 27b^2 = 216 = 1 mod 5 so the discriminant is nonzero, the affine points are (1, +-1) and (2, +-1), so #E(F_5) = 5, a_5 = 1, E is ordinary and E(F_5) = Z/5 is an etale subgroup scheme of order 5 distinct from ker F. The node builds a hypothesis and an acceptance test on the false sentence, and the fix -- supersingular versus ordinary, and Deligne's own two-component decomposition giving T_p = F + I_p^* V -- is the right repair. Limit: the Numdam scan of Bourbaki 355 (sha256 19509c19..., which reproduces) is page images here, so I could not read p. 157 or (4.7) myself; the attribution of the slip to Deligne rests on the node's own quotation of that sentence and on the red team's reading, which agree. Read in Chenevier's LaTeX source (arXiv:0809.0415v2 e-print). Theorem B in the introduction does carry 'Let A be a henselian local ring with algebraically closed residue field k', and the node's hypothesis is quoted verbatim from the decomposition, as is the open gap. Theorem 2.22 (label structurethm) assumes only 'Det is Cayley-Hamilton and A is henselian', and part (i) needs 'Det-bar is split and absolutely irreducible'; Definition 2.19 is verbatim 'We say that Det is split if it is the determinant of a representation R -> M_d(k). Equivalently, Det is split if and only if R/ker(Det) is a finite product of matrix algebras over k.' The added lemma is correct: if D-bar is absolutely irreducible then R-bar/ker(D-bar) is a central simple k-algebra of degree d, and over a finite field Wedderburn's theorem makes the Brauer group trivial, so it is M_d(k) and D-bar is split. A complete local noetherian Hecke algebra is henselian, so 2.22(i) applies directly and the planned descent step is unnecessary.
